title: John Donne and the Metaphysical poets: fleas, compasses and conceits

explain.say: Imagine trying to win an argument about love using a flea. Mark but this flea, says John Donne's speaker. Donne lived from 1572 to 1631, and his poems were printed only after his death. The panels follow the argument of The Flea.

explain.say: Look at the panels: the flea has bitten them both, so their bloods mix inside it, a kind of marriage, he says. She kills it anyway. Then the twist in the last panel: you lost nothing by killing it, so you will lose as little by giving in to me. Is that clever, or cheeky?

explain.say: That is a conceit, a far-fetched comparison worked out like a logical argument. Sort the moves Metaphysical poets make: wild conceits, sudden spoken openings like Busy old fool, unruly sun, and mixing love with faith. Samuel Johnson grumbled in 1779 that their ideas were yoked by violence together. Which move do you like best?

Donne's most famous conceit: leaving his wife for a journey, he compares the lovers to stiff twin compasses. Look at the board: she is the fixed foot at the centre, he is the moving foot, and her firmness makes his circle perfect, ending where it began. Why a compass and not a heart?

explain.say: Two verdicts. On the left, Johnson: forced and far-fetched. On the right, T. S. Eliot in 1921: these poets felt thought as directly as a scent, and modern poets should learn from them. Great thinking. Challenge: write a conceit comparing love to something in your bag.

faq.a: An extended, surprising comparison between very unlike things, argued out with logic and wit, like Donne's lovers as the two legs of a drawing compass.
Samuel Johnson fixed the label in his Life of Cowley in 1779, criticising their learned, far-fetched wit. The poets themselves never formed a group.
asks: Why are they called Metaphysical poets?

faq.a: A speaker tries to persuade a woman to sleep with him by arguing that a flea which has bitten them both has already mixed their blood. When she kills it, he turns her action into another argument.

faq.q: What does the compass image mean in A Valediction?
faq.a: The lovers are like the two legs of a drawing compass. The beloved stays at the centre while the traveller moves, and her firmness lets him complete the circle and return home.

faq.q: What did T. S. Eliot say about the Metaphysical poets?
faq.a: In a 1921 essay Eliot praised them for fusing thought and feeling, and argued that later English poetry had lost this unity. His essay revived their reputation.

facts: Donne's collected Poems were first published in 1633, two years after his death.
Donne became Dean of St Paul's Cathedral in 1621.
Other poets grouped as Metaphysical include George Herbert, Andrew Marvell and Henry Vaughan.
